notes:
Account summary: high-volume travel personalization + chat assistants across web + mobile. Very focused on production economics and predictable throughput. Procurement wants hard throughput guarantees (min tokens/sec) and clear burst behavior. Legal wants precise SLA fallback & remedies. SE running performance POC.

Key UX from meetings: 
- "We need predictable per-hour throughput during flash sales; token spikes are the killer." (CTO)
- Main ask: baseline guaranteed throughput + short burst headroom + rapid failover to regional capacity.

POC scope: 2-week performance POC against Novaseq-like load (~20k concurrent sessions simulated) with gen lengths up to 1024 tokens. Metrics to validate: tokens/sec sustained, p95 token latency, KV cache hit-rate, tail latency under burst.

Commercial: looking at 12-24 month reserved capacity; negotiating breach credit tiers (service credits, not just support).

throughput_requirements: Baseline guarantee: 1,500 tokens/sec sustained (per cluster) at concurrency of 24 generation streams for 1024-token sequences
Min tokens/sec per reserved unit: 375 tokens/sec per A100-80GB equivalent (baseline planning metric)
Concurrency caps: soft cap 48 concurrent active sessions per cluster, hard cap 96 with throttling/fair-share

Burst policy: allowed burst = up to 3x baseline sustained for up to 3 minutes every 15 minutes (burst smoothing enabled). Bursts beyond that must fall back to pre-agreed overflow region or reduced-quality model variant
SLA latency targets tied to throughput: p95 token latency <100ms during baseline; p99 <300ms with grace during bursts
KV/prefix cache behavior: cache warming window not to count against throughput SLA for first 5 minutes of a deployment roll
reserved_gpu_plan: Initial recommendation: 4x A100-80GB reserved (expected to meet baseline for typical traffic)
Growth plan: option to add 2x A100 every quarter for 12 months based on telemetry triggers
Alternative: price-request for 8x A40-48GB as a lower-cost option; Redwood SE to provide perf delta matrix
Burst capacity options: short-term burst pool (3x baseline) provisioned as shared burst nodes across customers; need contractual guarantee of availability windows
sla_negotiation_points: Definition of 'tokens/sec' for mixed workloads (chat + retrieval + rerank) - agreed test harness needed
Remedies: service credits tiered by duration and severity (target: credits up to 30% of monthly fee for sustained breach > 2 hours)
Measurement: Redwood to provide per-route/token-level telemetry and audit logs for disputes
Failover: explicit contractual obligation for automatic regional failover with max RTO 2 minutes for critical routes
Termination: right to terminate if repeated SLA breaches (3 breaches in 12 months) with phase-out support
commercial_notes: EmberFall price sensitive during travel flash sales windows (May, Nov). Prefers annual commit but needs quarterly scaling options. Interested in blended pricing model: reserved baseline + burst credits. Procurement pushed for clearer unit metrics (tokens per USD) and banded credit schedule.
